note: Set B's numbers are consistent with the stacked bars in Figure 2-9: total shear-layup thicknesses of about 45/40/35/30/25/20/15/10 mm across the span positions, plus plausible small glass_biax (~3 mm) and dominant medium_density_foam splits. Set A repeatedly binds total stack heights to glass_biax (42 mm at 25%, 45 mm at 15%, 32 mm at 44%, 12 mm at 100%, 38 mm at 33%) and foam-scale values to CarbonUD (23 mm at 54%, 13 mm at 77%), even though the carbon plies are only a thin bottom sliver. Set A also contradicts itself (glass_biax 1 vs 3 mm at 77%, 3 vs 4 mm at 64%) and adds trivial zero-Thickness CarbonUD claims for the empty circular 0%/2% positions. Set B's weakness is that its 'thickness' claims omit the layer (vague total-stack thickness) and it drops web0 at 64%, but nothing in it is clearly misbound.
remarks: Layer-segment values can only be estimated from the bar chart (no data labels), so fine splits (glass_biax 3 vs 4 mm, foam 25 vs 27 mm) are hard to verify; I penalized only claims that are impossible against the bar totals. The web0 and web1 panels look nearly identical, yet both sets give different web0/web1 values at the same span position (e.g. B: foam 13 vs 10 mm at 77%, 27 vs 25 mm at 44%) — worth checking against the source data. Both sets omit gelcoat, glass_triax and glass_uni layer thicknesses entirely.
